newsitem.title: INDIA: India to set rules for foreign investors in media.
newsitem.headline: India to set rules for foreign investors in media.

text.p: The Indian government said on Thursday that it would consider proposals for foreign investment in the information and broadcasting sectors after a new policy is announced on the subject.

"Since the new broadcasting law/policy is presently under the review of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, it has been decided that application for foreign investment in respect of any aspect of broadcasting will be entertained by the FIPB (Foreign Investment Promotion Board) only after the new policy is announced by the government," an official statement said.
It did not specify when the policy would be ready.
The FIPB is a panel of senior government officials attached to the Industry Ministry which can approve foreign investment up to six billion rupees.
